That's expected, as in initrd mounts specified in systemd.mount-extra= are only taken into account only if it is for `/` or `/usr`. Though, that's not documented. But the behavior is the same as how we handle system's fstab file in initrd phase.

> Hmm, I am pretty sure the non-prefixed kernel cmdline option should only be applied on the host, not the initrd. i.e. mount "rd." stuff only in initrd, and non-"rd." stuff only on host. Why that? simply because people might use this for loopback files or using fuse file systems which only work on the host because the files/infra only exists there. Trying to mount this ahead of time from the initrd sounds problematic hence, and likely wll result in failures.
> 
> Yes, I know we already released this, but I'd still change this.

@poettering and @keszybz 

I cannot follow. As commented in the above, currently mounts specified in systemd.mount-extra= are taken into account if it is only for `/` or `/usr`. That is, only necessary for switching root are mounted in initrd. The behavior is the same as how we handle system's fstab or `fstab.extra` creds.
If people wants to specify loopback block device, then that should be OK with the current form of the implementation. If people want to use loopback device as `/` or `/usr`, then the image must be accessible from initrd (same as fuse or so, people needs to install necessary files in initrd). There is nothing special. As if we want to mount btrfs from initrd, we need to install relevant kernel module and mount command into initrd. Conversely, if a loopback device is specified for non root or usr mount point, then it is completely ignored in initrd phase, and will be mounted after switching root.
I've not tested such setup, but loopback or fuse mount should also work in the current form, and I think there is nothing we need to 'revert' the change in this PR.

> fwiw in spite of what the documentation says I don't see mount units specified with `systemd.mount-extra=` being handled in the initrd on Fedora Rawhide with systemd-254.

did you rebuild the initrd with the new systemd inside it?

> I cannot follow. As commented in the above, currently mounts specified in systemd.mount-extra= are taken into account if it is only for `/` or `/usr`.

Ah, I didn't grok this. Makes sense then. (Though really documented, I guess)

It might make sense to introduce a proper "rd." prefix though

> > fwiw in spite of what the documentation says I don't see mount units specified with `systemd.mount-extra=` being handled in the initrd on Fedora Rawhide with systemd-254.
> 
> did you rebuild the initrd with the new systemd inside it?

Yes - I had the same misunderstanding that only `/` and `/usr` are handled in the initramfs, so that's behaving as I expected it.

> That's #28645 and already fixed.

Thanks! I just tested with the patches from #28645 and that fixes the problem for me.

Originally posted by @bmr-cymru in https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/27260#issuecomment-1649986565.


I'm trying to test the new `systemd.mount-extra` in Fedora Rawhide with systemd-254~rc3-1.fc39.x86_64 and LVM2 logical volumes and I'm running into some problems.

Firstly, when using command line mount units and `nofstab` nothing pulls in `systemd-remount-fs.service`, which leaves the root fs mounted read-only: I think that unit should be pulled in if command line or credentials fstab entries are present. Other than that the basic case of booting a system with the fstab entries on the kernel command line seems to work as expected:

```
root=/dev/fedora/root ro rd.lvm.lv=fedora/root rd.lvm.lv=fedora/var rd.lvm.lv=fedora/home fstab=no systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/root:/:ext4:rw systemd.mount-extra=/dev/vda2:/boot:ext4:defaults systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/var:/var:ext4:defaults systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/home:/home:ext4:defaults
```

The system boots normally and file systems are mounted as expected:

```
# grep fedora /proc/mounts 
/dev/mapper/fedora-root / ext4 ro,seclabel,relatime 0 0
/dev/mapper/fedora-home /home ext4 rw,seclabel,relatime 0 0
/dev/mapper/fedora-var /var ext4 rw,seclabel,relatime 0 0
```

Attempting to boot into a snapshot of the system state fails unpredictably: in some cases the system appears to boot normally but systemd attempts to unmount the command line mounts after switching root. In other cases the devices for the command line mount units time out. I'm struggling to debug this: the generated unit files seem sane and I can't figure out why the umounts and timeouts are occurring.

The snapshot command line looks like this:

```
root=/dev/fedora/root-snap ro rd.lvm.lv=fedora/root-snap rd.lvm.lv=fedora/var-snap rd.lvm.lv=fedora/home-snap fstab=no systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/root-snap:/:ext4:rw systemd.mount-extra=/dev/vda2:/boot:ext4:defaults systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/var-snap:/var:ext4:defaults systemd.mount-extra=/dev/fedora/home-snap:/home:ext4:defaults

comments:
Thanks! Does this have to do with the mount units being generated in the initramfs? I noticed in the logs that the command line mount units are interleaved with the mount of /sysroot (in the logs above dm-8 (/var) and dm-12 (/home) appear to be mounted *before* /sysroot??). This contrasts with normal boots where the auxiliary filesystems are all mounted after the switchroot.

I noticed that `add_mounts_from_cmdline()` always passes `initrd=false` which disables the `mount_in_initrd()` test in `parse_fstab_one()`. That means that all command line mount units will be mounted from the initrd regardless of the presence of `x-initrd.mount` in the mount options. That seems wrong.

Would it be better to have `add_mounts_from_cmdline()` also test `in_initrd()` and pass the `initrd` parameter to `parse_fstab_one()` accordingly? That way mounts that lack `x-initrd.mount`/are not `/usr` will be skipped over in the initramfs as with normal fstab processing.

Fix is waiting in #28518.
If it does not work, please provide generated units.
Thank you! I am building packages with the patches from #28518 now and I will update after testing.
